elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised 20(d) permits consent-free assignment only "to a successor to its business upon written notice"; no affiliate carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered language, so an affiliate transfer still falls into the "any other assignment requires the written consent" bucket.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised 20(d): "Either party may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business upon written notice to the other party"; the conflicting prohibition in 3(c) was deleted so Sparkling (Customer) is no longer barred from assigning.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The successor right is mutual ("Either party"), so Garman (Vendor) may assign to a successor to its business on notice alone, without Customer consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Revised 20(d): "any other assignment requires the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar exists in the rendered text; Vendor's successor assignment right is unqualified as to the identity of the transferee.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the Agreement contains no change-of-control clause and no Vendor termination or re-pricing trigger on Customer's change of control, and the redline introduces none.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Revised 20(d): "Either party may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business..."; the retained words in 3(c) that would have barred Sparkling from assigning were struck, so no contradictory sentence survives.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Revised 20(d): "...to a successor to its business upon written notice to the other party".
Revised 20(d): "any other assignment requires the written consent of the other party"; no residual no-consent non-successor exception (no affiliate or subcontracting exception) is retained anywhere.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Revised 20(d): consent "shall not be unreasonably withheld."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: mutual successor assignment on written notice, all other assignments subject to consent not unreasonably withheld.

Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate carve-out for Customer, the successor right is mutual (so Vendor can assign without Customer consent), and there is no bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. If the preferred position is pursued, add (i) "Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets", (ii) restrict the consent-free successor right to Sparkling only, and (iii) add "and in no event to a competitor of Sparkling".

The deletion of "assign this Agreement or" from Section 3(c) is necessary, not cosmetic: retained, that covenant would flatly contradict the new mutual successor right and reinstate a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment. The remainder of 3(c) (transfer, lease, export, sublicence of the Work) is preserved intact and reads grammatically within the covenant list.
No dangling cross-references or undefined terms result; the change-of-control analysis is unaffected because the Agreement contains no such trigger.

Minor drafting note only (not a level failure): the rewrite of 20(d) drops the original words "or any rights and obligations under this Agreement". "Any other assignment" should be read to capture partial transfers, but if the counterparty may argue otherwise, restore breadth with "any other assignment or transfer of rights or obligations requires the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."
